key_insight: How knowledge is ordered during pre-training changes later update efficiency: models trained chronologically become "specialists" that adapt to new knowledge much faster than randomly shuffled "generalists."
engineering_relevance: For continually updated language models, pre-training data organization can reduce future update cost while helping preserve useful historical knowledge.
method: Compare chronological vs randomly shuffled pre-training knowledge orderings.
Derive a first-principles law linking update cost to optimization dynamics.
Design a data-ordering strategy that improves stability of past knowledge and update efficiency for current knowledge.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports empirical comparisons on pre-trained models and existing knowledge-update tools, with the derived law closely predicting observed update costs across knowledge orderings.
watch_item: The benefit depends on temporal structure in the training data, so gains may be weaker or require re-tuning when the data does not have a meaningful chronology.
paper_title: Specialists Learn Faster: Knowledge Organization in Pre-training Shapes Knowledge Update Efficiency
